messages:
mariam: heads up — nightly finops dashboard shows a ~43% spike in per-route cost for `embed-route-prod` in us-west1 around 02:10 UTC last night. tagging looks off on several GPU nodes, cost attributed to 'unlabeled' instead of route. @jonathan @adele can you take a quick look? :eyes:

jonathan: saw that alert too. I ran `gcloud billing accounts costs --start=2026-03-16T02:00 --end=2026-03-16T03:00 --group-by=label` and there's a big chunk under `no_label`. Thinking autoscaler rollout yesterday removed the node label `route=embed-prod` on the newer nodepool. rolling back that autoscaler change now.

billing-bot: Billing alert: cost anomaly detected for project/redwood-us-west1 — +42% hour-over-hour at 2026-03-16T02:12 UTC. Estimated incremental cost: $6,200. Ticket: FIN-4521.

srini: quick datapoint — model usage shifted last night: embed requests spiked and average seq_len went from 128 -> 412 for a 45m window (likely batch job). That would increase token cost even with correct labeling. both factors probably contributed.

adele: confirmed via `kubectl get nodes -L route` — 7/27 nodes in the pool returned `<none>` for label. My guess is the node-template change removed `nodeLabels` on instance creation. Patch ready, applying now.

mariam: can we retro-run cost attribution for the unlabelled chunk so we map to routes? Need to show customers + ops impact before we close FIN-4521. Also want to check if reserved capacity assignments were affected (did traffic spill to on-demand GPUs?).

jonathan: good call. I kicked off a BigQuery job to reclassify `no_label` by matching VM instance ids in billing export to Kubernetes node names and pods (using last seen tag). Query id: bq_job_20260316_relabel_01. Estimated runtime 12m. If that maps most of the $6.2k to `embed-route-prod` we can attribute to route and adjust internal chargeback.

billing-bot: bq_job_20260316_relabel_01 completed: 88% of `no_label` cost mapped to `embed-route-prod`, 9% to `search-route`, 3% unknown. Results uploaded to gs://redwood-finops/ FIN-4521/relabel_results.csv

srini: re: reserved capacity — logs show no Dedicated pool preemptions, but autoscaler fallback caused a short (~9m) burst to on-demand GPUs in us-west1 due to nodepool scaling delay. That on-demand window accounts for ~15% of the anomaly.

adele: created infra PR to enforce `nodeLabels: {route: <pool-route>}` in the instance template and added a presubmit that checks for label drift. Also added a quick remediation script to reapply labels for existing nodes: `scripts/fix-node-labels.sh`.

mariam: great. action items: 1) jonathan will attach relabel CSV to FIN-4521 and run cost re-attribution (due EOD), 2) adele will merge the infra PR and run the remediation script (done in next 30m), 3) srini to confirm reserved pool usage/commitment impact and estimate incremental on-demand cost (tomorrow morning).

jonathan: attaching results now and will kick the chargeback job: `./tools/chargeback/reassign_costs --input relabel_results.csv --date 2026-03-16`

adele: PR merged and remediation run: `kubectl label node <node> route=embed-prod --overwrite` (ran on 20 nodes). No further unlabeled nodes after fix.

mariam: thanks team. final ask — add a dashboard card that alerts when >5% of hour cost is `no_label` so we catch this earlier. small query suggestion: `SUM(cost) FILTER(label IS NULL)/SUM(cost) > 0.05`.

jonathan: will add the alert to FinOps dashboard, threshold 3% with a 15m window.

srini: noted, I'll also add a model-side guard to limit auto-batch/context expansion for background jobs during low-priority windows to avoid surprise seq_len spikes.

mariam: closing the thread for now — FIN-4521 updated with chargeback adjustments and remediation notes. follow-up in weekly finops sync. :white_check_mark:
